notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0034.stoa001.opp-la: A stray 'f.' stands in the Latin before 'siue illi mares', apparently a marginal mark; not translated. 'sacrorum libaminum temporum' lacks a connective and may be corrupt; taken as 'sacred libations [and] times'.

nodes.text: He will perhaps meet us again with many other slanderous and childish words: 'He was a magician; he accomplished all those things by secret arts; from the shrines of the Egyptians he stole the names of powerful angels and abstruse disciplines.' What are you saying, you little ones, prattling with the garrulity of a rash voice about things unascertained and unknown to you? Were those things that were done, then, the illusions of demons and the tricks of magic arts? Can you point out to us, show [us], anyone out of all those magicians who have ever existed through the ages who did anything at all like Christ, even to a thousandth part? Who [did it] without any force of spells, without the juices of herbs and grasses, without any anxious observance of sacred libations [and] times? For we do not press and inquire what they promise to do, or in what kinds of acts all their teaching and experience is usually contained. For who does not know that these people either strive to know beforehand impending things, which come of necessity by their own ordering whether they will or not; or send a deadly wasting on whomever they please; or break apart the affections of families; or open without keys what is closed; or bind mouths with silence; or in the races weaken, urge on, or slow down horses; or send into other men's wives and children, whether they are male or of the female sex, the flames of forbidden love and frenzied desires; or, if they seem to venture anything useful, that they can do it not by their own power but by the power of those whom they invoke?
